game: WAS@LAC Week 5 2025, kickoff 2025-10-05 16:25 ET, SoFi dome

script.base: Dome, LAC -2.5, total 47.5, implied LAC 25.0 / WAS 22.5. Books expect a close game with a late LAC lead, not a blowout (spread under 3.5). Herbert throws into a WAS secondary that has bled every zone (left 8.02, middle 8.41, right 9.3 YPA; 13 passes of 20+). Hampton (39 car / 222 yds over weeks 2-4) is the closer if LAC leads. Mariota, with McLaurin and Brown out and Cosmi out, leans short/middle to Samuel and Ertz; the WAS backfield stays a committee (Croskey-Merritt 19/90, Rodriguez 18/98, Mariota 8/60, Ekeler 8/17).
script.flip1: LAC gets up early, clocks Hampton, and WAS abandons the run so Croskey-Merritt and Rodriguez rush lines die while Ertz, Samuel and McCaffrey targets spike. If the lead becomes a real blowout, Najee can vulture fourth-quarter carries — that is the kill path for a Najee rush under.
script.flip2: WAS hangs or leads and both teams throw in the dome. Hampton's rush stalls, Johnston/Allen/Ertz/Samuel yardage rises together, and Najee's already-small carry share shrinks further.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game nflverse report, not the 90-minute inactive list (not in pack). WAS WR Terry McLaurin OUT (quad) and WR Noah Brown OUT (groin) remove the downfield WR (McLaurin 13 tgt / 122 yds / 167 air in weeks 2-4) and a secondary WR. Targets funnel to Deebo Samuel (17/127/80), Zach Ertz (15/123/114), Luke McCaffrey (7/96/83) and Jaylin Lane (9/18/87). WAS G Sam Cosmi OUT (knee) should raise pressure, cut rush efficiency and push quick throws (TE/RB catches up, deep yards down — the deep threat is already out). LAC T Joe Alt OUT (ankle) weakens the OL for Hampton efficiency and Herbert's deep timing. LAC WR Derius Davis OUT (knee) is a gadget/returner loss, not a target vacuum (Johnston 29, Allen 25, McConkey 18 already own the shares). LAC TE Will Dissly Q (knee), TE Tucker Fisk Q (toe), G Mekhi Becton Q (concussion) are not ruled out; do not treat them as sleepers until inactives.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting, MOFO/MOFC or man/zone rate in the pack. Proxy only: LAC blitzes just 24% and allows 8.46 YPA up the middle (28 att) vs 5.17 left (48) and 4.41 right (51), so the bleed is hook/middle, not the outside corners. WAS blitzes 32% and has been gashed on the perimeter (right 9.3 YPA on 54 att).
matchup.pressure: LAC pressure is not charted beyond a 24% blitz. WAS EPA/dropback is better vs blitz (0.25) than clean (0.00), but LAC rarely blitzes, and Cosmi out is the pressure risk for Mariota — more checkdowns, fewer deep shots. Herbert's EPA/dropback is fine vs WAS's 32% blitz (0.15 vs blitz, 0.03 clean), so pressure alone does not kill LAC's pass game; Alt out is the separate OL concern.
matchup.bleeds: LAC defense bleeds the middle (8.46 YPA) and is only average vs the run (4.55 YPC, 16 runs of 10+, just 8 passes of 20+ for 140). WAS defense bleeds the pass everywhere, worst to the right (9.3) and on explosives (13 of 20+ for 133), while the run front is the sturdy piece (3.85 YPC, 11 runs of 10+). Position-allowed splits (WR1/slot/TE/RB) are not in the pack.
matchup.overlap: With McLaurin out, WAS's best overlap is Ertz (15 targets, 114 air yards, TE in the middle) into LAC's middle bleed, plus Samuel's short/hook work (80 air on 17 targets). LAC's primary overlap is Johnston's air-yard load (29 tgt / 371 air / 258 yds) into a WAS secondary that allows explosives on every side — real, but his 84.5 line sits on his own median, so it is not the soft number.

form: Avoiding season averages; weeks 2-4 sums and listed last-4 lines only. Ertz 123 yds on 15 targets (~41/game) vs a 32.5 line; last4 recyds 26, 64, 38, 21 (split, not a rising trend, and those games still included McLaurin). Samuel 127 on 17 (~42/game) vs 58.5; last4 77, 44, 11, 72 — line is above the recent mean even before pricing the McLaurin bump. McCaffrey 96 on only 7 targets is spike-inflated (last4 19, 56, 21 vs 21.5). Lane 9 targets for 18 yards, unplayable efficiency. Johnston last4 79, 71, 89, 98 vs 84.5 (median on the number; L3 ~86/game). Allen L3 ~54/game vs a 63.5 line (last4 68, 61, 65, 37). McConkey trending 74, 48, 41, 11, L3 ~33 vs 44.5. Hampton rush last4 48, 24, 70, 128 vs 59.5, L3 74/game on 13 carries, against a 3.85 YPC WAS front — form and matchup disagree. Najee rush last4 5, 28, 28, all under 28.5, on 14 carries / 56 yards behind Hampton. Rodriguez's two listed games (39, 59) average the 49.5 line; no gap.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Ertz lost because LAC finally protected the middle, Mariota's Cosmi-less quick game stuck on Deebo and the backs, and Ertz posted another 21-yard afternoon while McCaffrey's one explosive catch stole the vacated McLaurin shot — the last4 already showed that floor twice, and we never had a coverage chart to prove the middle would stay open. Najee lost because Hampton exited or LAC led by two scores and the backup closed with 30-plus garbage yards, or because one of WAS's 11 allowed 10-plus runs was his. The counter-case is real on Ertz's split form and on Najee's blowout flip; it is not stronger than the base read, so both stay, flagged where the numbers disagree.
slip_story: One competitive-dome story, not a shootout stack and not a clock-kill stack: WAS's pass game without McLaurin funnels to the TE (Ertz recyds over) while LAC's RB2 stays capped behind Hampton against a good WAS run front (Najee rushyds under). Those two win together in the base script and in the WAS-leads flip. Do not add Hampton rush over, a WAS RB over, or a total under — those need the other script. Two legs, no TDs, one market per player. McConkey under and Allen under were average-driven and fight the WAS pass bleed, so they are not on the slip. Johnston over is the right overlap but the 84.5 rung is his median, a lean the split last4 does not confirm, so it is dropped rather than forced.
